Hyunseoan expansion into Soyo.
An main land territory with  a weak government with around 310.000 people living in it, the capital, or better saying, largest city is Hwiparam, a city with white limestone cliffs that echo in the wind.
The Soyo republic was a presidential republic which suffered from a terrible political crisis, within the last 20 years prior the annexation, the country having over 11 presidents due to impeachments, depositions, renouncements...and while they were failing, the people only wished for better security and less corruption, as the local infrastructure would fall into decadence, while the Hyunseoans would thrive.

The Soyo economic.

Economically, Soyo always lived in the shadow of Hyunseo. The larger archipelago was the dominant trading partner, buying fish, limestone, and offering tourists in exchange for electronics, ships, and manufactured goods. There was economic dependence, but also cultural rivalrythe Soyoans saw themselves as a more "old" and "authentic" nation, while the Hyunseans considered the Soyoans provincial and old-fashioned mainlanders.
[b]Hyungnae user, Seo Han-gyeol and plans[/b].
A 14 years old boy, with slim body and shoulder length wavy black hair with his thick eyebrows seeming always to be arched.
The government had found him in a school of Soyo, a hyunseoan exchange student , and contacted him, he already had the musi-hyungnae in hands when he was found, the ministry of intelligence contacted him...
Seo Han-gyeol didn't look like an intelligence agent. He looked like a bored exchange student, sitting in the Ministry waiting room with a book of Soyoana poetry open on his lap, his dark eyes scanning the pages with the same blank attention he would give to an instruction manual. Slightly paler skin than most Hyunseoans. Wavy shoulder-length black hair, thick eyebrows that are necessarily arched in silent judgment. He was wearing a worn-out school coat. The agent accompanying him was a man named Kang, who had made the initial contact, went ahead of him and asked the question that the Ministry dismissed. 
 [i]Let's say, in a hypothetical situation, we order you to infiltrate somewhere, create ties and, suddenly, kill some of these people. Would you obey? [/i]
Han-gyeol didn't hesitate. He didn't take a deep breath. The answer came with the same flat intonation he would use to ask for more tangerines:
  [i]Yes. They were never my friends to begin with. [/i]Kang, a forty-year-old man who had seen things that kept him from sleeping, felt a chill running down his spine. It wasn't an answer. It was the absence of anything that should come before the answer. No conflict. No consideration. No spark of humanity to suggest those words cost anything. 
[i]Do you understand what you're saying? 
I understand.[/i]
 [i]And still[/i]? 
Han-gyeol closed the book with his long pale fingers moving next to the book cover. 
[i]You are asking me if I have scruples. The answer is no. Is this a problem?[/i]
 Kang didn't respond. He got up, left the room and made the report.
 "Active suitable. I recommend immediate use. I also recommend never leaving it unattended."
 The Minister read the report, then looked at the attached photo. A fourteen-year-old boy with eyes that have already clarified every question and found every answer empty. 
Approved."
....
....
....
By simply becoming a "friend" of a Minister's son, Han-Gyeol used this as an opportunity to seize the identity of the minister Min Jao, however, this would not end there, Gyeol used this as an opportunity to meet with the president Park, and handshake, which inevitably, led to him also seizing his identity....
...
07th March 2015.
Kang would be the one to be sent as to neutralize the minister Jao, but, when he entered his office Min Jao lay on the floor, arms slightly outstretched, as if frozen mid-gesture. A thin, precise line ran across his neck, too clean to be called violent, too deliberate to be anything else.
Han-gyeol stood nearby, still wearing the ministers face.
He turned his head slightly when Kang entered, his expression unchanged, his eyes flat.
[i]You are late[/i].
Kang stopped at the doorway. For a moment, he couldnt move, couldnt speak. His gaze shifted between the body on the floor and the boy standing before himno, not a boy anymore, not in any sense that mattered.
[i]I I came to handle this[/i].
Kang said, his voice unsteady despite years of training. 
[i]I infiltrated this place to spare your youth. I believed you wouldnt be able to kill.[/i]
Han-gyeol watched him in silence for a second, then stepped away from the body.
[i]You asked me if I could kill. Yes, I can. In fact, I joined your government for that purpose. Either I'm fourteen, forty, whatever..[/i]
Kangs expression tightened.
Han-gyeol reached up and lightly brushed his fingers across his own face. The features shiftedsubtly at first, then completelyuntil Minister Jao stood there in full.
[i]Killing is a rather[/i]...
 he continued.
 [i]Adequate, for the kind of him, won't you agree?[/i]
He walked past Kang, close enough that their shoulders nearly touched, but not quite.
[i]What on Erene are you intending now?[/i]
Han-gyeol paused at the doorway.
[i]The President is Ill and I already handshaked with him, I'm slowly trying to integrate Soyo into Hyunseo, your government wished for mainland territory didn't it.[/i]
Kang turned and his eyes eyes widened slightly. 
[i]You what[/i]-
Han-gyeol raised a hand, transforming himself into the 14 years old boy he was, the black long hair would return and his body return, the only problem being the size of the Minister's cloth though.
Silence filled the room again, heavier this time.
Kang looked at the body on the floor, then back at the boy, who had already started walking away.
...
...
President Park really died of a heartattack about 2 months after Minister Jao's, but, his body was quickly taken away, as Kang tried to give his best to cover for the young agent, the people did not complained even a little as the president acted "weird", in fact the population was rather...satisfied, they gave up of really believing the country would have any future, and even praised the president:
[i]So the president awake up to reality?[/i]
...after a plebiscite at June 18th 2015, the Soyo republic was to be fully integrated into Hyunseo, min-ulwon representatives joined, the people fully integrated as hyunseoan citizens, and everything of Soyo was naturally integrated into Hyunseo, with no special status.
....
[b]Today:[/b]
Currently Seo Han-gyeol is an agent of 26 years old, the youngest Senior Agent in the ministry of intelligence, and acts as a agent for the Hyunseo government investigations, espionage, and assassinations, he trained well to become a well talented combatant in a direct fight and to immobilize his opponents.
[b]Ministry of Intelligence  Break Room, Seonhang[/b]
Seo Han-gyeol sat on the worn leather couch, one leg folded under him, a book of Soyoan folk tales open on his lap. His black hair, still wavy, still too long, fell over one eye. He didn't bother pushing it back.
Across from him, agent Chae Yoo-na sat on the edge of the table, peeling a tangerine with the focused attention of someone defusing a bomb. She is twenty-nine, sharp-faced, with a reputation for being among the only people in the  building who could consistently talk genuinely with the young senior agent, but not the only.
[I]You're reading that again, she said, tossing a segment into her mouth.[/I]
[i]It's calming.[/i]
[i]It's propaganda. The old Soyoan stories are half myths about resisting Hyunseoan influence.
[/i]
Han-gyeol turned a page.
[i]Myths exist far more than politics you know.[/I]
Yoo-na considered this, then shrugged. She finished her tangerine and leaned back, wiping her hands on her pants.
[i]You know what I think?[/i]
[i]You're going to tell me regardless.[/i]
I [i]think you like them because they're sad.[/i]
He looked up at that, his thick eyebrows lifting just slightly. Not offended, simply curious.
[i]Sad[/i] you say.
[i]The Soyoan folk tales. They're all about waiting. People waiting for the wind to change, waiting for the sea to return what it took, you like things that wait...way too much to be fair.[/i]
Han-gyeol closed the book, keeping his finger between the pages.
[i]That's not why.[/i]
He answered looking at her with the side of his eye.
Then why?
He tilted his head, thinking with a hand on his chin.
[i]They're honest, that's all.[/i]
Yoo-na rolled her eyes.
[i]Come on this is just the same thing but in different words![/i]
[i]It's not .[/i]
he said, and for a moment there was something almost warm in his voice, [i]almost[/i]. 
[i]Sadness is a feeling. Honesty is just... not lying to yourself about how things are.[/i]
She stared at him for a long second, then reached over and stole a segment of tangerine from the bowl on the table.
[i]You're weird, Gyeol.[/i]
[i]You're only realizing this now?[/i]
[i]No[/i]
 she admitted and proceeded:
[i]I just like saying it.[/i]

[b]The Dhora Communist Party[/b]

The overall results of Operation Misericordia would produce fairly mixed results. 

In a brief summary, those communists who were considered to be of particularly high value, whether due to their senior positions within the Dhora communist movement or otherwise deep and underappreciated mind for revolutionary politics, constituted the majority of rescues in the great seas. Other communists who've flown under the radar, or who could much more easily disguise themselves, or were otherwise unknown to Dhora authorities, were better capable of fleeing legally via international flights to sympathetic countries or through the tense northern border zone guarded by Socintern militia men.

While official numbers would be kept under wraps, the Conference of Discussions of the Socintern would roughly estimate successful rescues at around 212 for all groupings of Red émigrés, and around 25 for the most politically-important members of the communist movement. This was, in of itself, nothing to make fun of, and even the smallest, most insignificant filaments of light are capable of blazing brilliantly into an all-consuming fire. Take the Min Zhu Party as an example, which during its onset could only provide 11 delegates representing 71 members in the aftermath of the Tianci Uprising.

However, to the dismay of the Socialist International, the actual grouping of Red émigrés would not be fully homogenous. Instead, having lacked serious native communist movements of their own, the Dhora communist leadership expressed a wide and seemingly irreconciliable range of political ideologies. To merge all of these men and women under a single political movement and a single central committee would be effectively the suicide of the entire Dhora left through ideological paralyis. And yet, the International would not, and simply could not purge the people it had saved for fear of unwittingly dooming the entire Dhora left especially now with the final institutionalization of monarcho-fascism in Dhornaper.

Just as they were many reasons to differentiate between the notable members of the Dhora communist movement from one another, there were also several different reasons that the wider movement could be differentiate from the orthodox line of the Socialist International. At a plenary session at Citharo, key statements would be made by three delegates:

[list][b][u]Cui Fang[/u][/b]: "At the present moment, we have identified two specific factions within the Dhora communist movement. The first are the [i]Derafshiyan[/i] "standard-bearers" under Comrade Kourosh Ghahreman, while the second are the [i]Fadayan[/i] "self-sacrificers" under Comrade Siamak Raminfar. Both of these factions cannot work with each other, but work remarkably well within their own respective camps. Those that call themselves Derafshiyan derive their cause from the saying [i]Derafshi shodan[/i] (درفشی شدن), that is, "to become a banner", for they believe that the purpose of the revolutionary struggle is for the individual members and delegates to transform themselves into a visible banner enlightening the masses to the necessity of armed struggle against monarcho-fascism. It is my belief that the Derafshiyan may have been the faction responsible for the dissemination of the early adventurist pamphlets that led to the monarcho-fascist crackdowns, but have not been responsible for any further agitation, and are notable for their commitment both to Islamic socialism and gradualist politics. The [i]Fadayan[/i] are a militant league who share their name with the various irregular militia movements and resistance groups in Shamatine history, all of whom presumably trace their etymological roots to the [i]fida'iyin[/i] employed by the historic Order of Assassins. We believe that the Fadayan were responsible for earlier and latter attacks on the Dhora state, as in the controversial assassination attempt on the Shah at the mosque earlier this week. The cause of the Fadayan is intrinsically linked to armed struggle, but they deviate immensely from the Citharo line by rejecting the protracted people's war, instead promoting immediate and highly propagandistic acts of terror to inspire the masses in revolt against the monarcho-fascist order. Both factions deviate significantly in their own way, yet we honor their sacrifices and their efforts to awaken the masses in their own way. But they cannot co-exist, not until a common cause between the camps has been established."

[b][u]Immacolata Terrasi[/u][/b]: "We believe that both camps have some Li'ist influence, at least concerning economic theories. This influence is most pronounced in the Fadayan, who reject the two-stage model adopted at the First Conference of Discussions, but in fact both factions carry suspicions towards the use of capitalism and the bourgeoisie to accomplish the initial tasks of the people's democratic state such as democracy and land reform. Comrade Raminfar has been the most explicit in articulating these views, as in his seminal work [i]Nejat-e Mardom[/i] ("The People's Freedom"), in which he stated that the purpose of the revolution was to immediately seize the means of production in the aftermath of the revolution to rapidly build up productive forces in a socialist planned economy. Comrade Javad Raminfar, who is Comrade Siamak's brother, is further believed to be a mainline Li'ist, for he fully rejects the necessity of foreign trade and association, instead believing that total autarky can be implemented within a single nation to immediately see the withering of the state. The Derafshiyan are similarly skeptics of the two-stage model, with Comrade Kourosh Ghahreman in particular advocating for New Order politics such as in the organization of the soviets, though he has since become more forthcoming to the necessity for the maturation of capitalism, and so we are optimistic at least that their faction will be more willing to shed its Li'ist, opportunistic influences."

[b][u]Argo Lo Pilato[/u][/b]: "Culturally, the Dhora communist movement remains explicitly nationalistic in character. Comrade Kourosh for example structures their camp along classical Dhora traditions of [i]adab[/i] (etiquette). There's a sense of poetic subtlety in discussions of a range of topics ranging from grand debates and discussions on the merits of the revolutionary cause to mundane things such as merely asking for promotion within a certain line of work. The Derafshiyan are quite explicit for example in operating their camp as a [i]khanedan[/i] ("household"), in which loyalty flows upwards from the junior cadres to the senior party leadership of its central committee. Comrade Kourosh in particular is treated with immense respect and often called "Brother Kourosh" at plenary sessions of the Derafshiyan. Comparatively, the Fadayan shed many of these cultural characteristics, instead organizing their respective society along adherence to the concept of [i]qahr[/i] or "righteous fury", that is, to mobilize through directness and collectivism to supercharge the masses through messianic revolutionary fervor. The Fadayan do not hold formally-organized central committee sessions, instead a network of spontaneous [i]maljes[/i] that mirror loud gatherings at a rural [i]hoy[/i] or urban [i]mahalleh[/i]. Even the simple act of party registration tends toward the theatrical, as in one case I witnessed in Wali Zurayq, in which a Fadai organized a mass swearing of the revolutionary oath over bread and salt."[/list]

For these multitudes of reasons, it was decided that the Dhora communist movement needed to be split along two separate camps, each with their own central committee, politburo, and formal statement of policies. Those espousing the more moderate mainline obedient to the Socintern's policies would be organized into the "Dhora Communist Party (Derafshi)", whereas hardliners and Li'ists would be organized into the "Dhora Communist Party (Fadai)", and would be given the power to register their own members and appoint their own delegates to represent them in the Socintern's Conference of Discussions.

At last count, the Derafshiyan would constitute the majority bloc among the Dhora communists, with a total of 15 delegates representing 115 members compared to the Fadayan who currently present 10 delegates for 72 members. As had been already identified in the key statements, the Derafshiyan would be led by Dhora intellectual Kourosh Ghahreman, while the Fadayan would be led by student activist Siamak Raminfar. The mean age of members across all camps would be remarkably low at just around 21 years old, mostly thanks to the student-led characteristics of both camps combined with natural biases arising from the immense physical exertion that had been necessary in their rescues.

After further deliberations, it would also be agreed to organize the Dhora into an organized military formation that was to operate within the structure of the International Columns, Socintern's main military organization. This new formation would be called the "Dhora Legion", and would operate at the company-level as a component of the Astaniran Democratic Army. Former army officer Mehdi Kuchak would be assigned to task as the Legion's first commander, and would be ordered stationed at Astanir to take up tasks with Pax International.

In the meantime, both Dhora factions would make their first appearance at the Socintern's plenary session, with many attendees suspecting that the International may seek to organize them into an alternative government to the Shah's monarcho-fascist government in due time.

[spoiler= The Destiny of the Aoka
[sub]Expansion Post Section I[/sub]]

The Sengoku Jidai was the most turbulent time throughout all of the Harmonious State's long history. The warring states period started in 1450 and lasted until 1626. During this time the many clans which made up the ancient Shogunate system fractured and began fighting for power and prestige. There were times of peace during the Sengoku Jidai, most notable the  ten (10) years between 1545 - 1555 saw no bloodshed. But it wasn't until 1626 when the armies of Emperor Kōshin would finally defeat the last of the unruly warlords and unite the nation in its entirety. It is still unknown to this day how many passed during the one hundred and seventy six (176) years of near constant conflict. But the times lead to what would become the Golden Age of thought and philosophy within Aokashima. In the late stages of the Sengoku Jidai, and the years directly following it, many great thinkers would arise. These great philosophers would spread their teachings around the nation, looking to create the changes that they wanted to see. However, none of these men were more influential than Sōma Tetsuryū, the [i]"Founding Philosopher"[/i]. The man who created the name "The Harmonious State."

Sōma Tetsuryū taught the Aokajin (Aoka People) that [i]"strength is the guarantor of peace".[/i] This has been a fundamental teaching that laid deep in the minds of the Aokajin ever since the end of the Sengoku Jidai. Ever since the end of that nasty saga, the Aokajin have always ensured that they were always stronger than anything which could threaten their peace. As it stands the Aokajin have not seen a war in over two hundred years, but it is not because they're weary of war. Nor is it because they are ill-prepared or unknowledgeable in modern war. Sōma Tetsuryū also taught that [i]"peace is not the evidence of weakness, but the evidence of power unused by the mighty".[/i] The Aokajin have lived for many years with powerful nations all around them, weary at any time their peace could be threatened. It is because of these outside factors that the Aokajin have ensured that they're ready for anything and everything that could happen. This readiness was seen shortly after the Sengoku Jidai when, instead of disbanding the Samurai forces which fought and burned their villages. They instead allowed them to keep their arms and enter the emperor's service, forming the first true United army of Aokashima. Not long after purpose built warships were created to ensure that Aokashima was protected from seaborn threats, forming the first united Navy of Aokashima. The ideas surrounding the usage of these forces were sharpened and honed through peacetime, and of course, through the teachings of Sōma Tetsuryū. His wisdom helped the first Emperor create the Aokashima which exists today, and his teachings are still taught today as the basis of Aokajin society. 

This high degree of readiness was not specific to the Armed Forces of Aokashima, it exists in every part of Aokajin society. Sōma Tetsuryū's teachings continuously repeat the idea that the betterment of the self is the betterment of society. When an individual acts selflessly, puts others first, and understands how be ambitious and humble, the nation benefits. All are expected to do their part in contributing to the nation's united success. Companies are expected to do things in a sustainable way, paving the way for a future where the young adults of tomorrow do not have to solve climate issues. Students are expected to learn so that they themselves can educate the next generation of their families. Individuals who serve the nation, be it as a politician, police officer, firefighter, military servicemember, or in other ways are expected to be knowledgeable professionals about their line of work, and the issues they will be asked to solve. The Harmonious State is a strict meritocracy, where those who prove themselves to be meritorious and capable will reap the rewards of their efforts. 

[/spoiler]

[spoiler= The Prefectures of Aokashima
[sub]Expansion Post Section II[/sub]]

The following is a list of the Prefectures of the Harmonious State of Aokashima, and their legal classification. There are five classifications for prefectures. These classifications are based on a few factors; they are as follows:

Tier I - Tier I prefectures are the irreplaceable heart of Aokashima. They contain the largest urban centers, key political institutions, major economic hubs, or central military infrastructure. These regions are highly resilient, self-sufficient, and capable of withstanding substantial disruption.

Tier II - Tier II prefectures are crucial for the nations economy, logistics, or strategic reach, though slightly less central or self sufficient than Tier I. They often contain important manufacturing hubs, resource-rich areas, or overseas economic assets.

Tier III - Tier III prefectures are contributors to the national economy or strategic system, but individually they are more replaceable or less resilient. These regions usually specialize in agriculture, resource extraction, or medium-scale manufacturing.

Tier IV - Tier IV prefectures are lightly populated, contributing to the nation in a limited way. But these smaller prefectures are close to the mainland. 

Tier V - Tier V prefectures are far from the mainland, and sparsely populated. They are often difficult to sustain but carry strategic or scientific value.

[spoiler= The "New Admissions" to Aokashima
[sub]Expansion Post Section III[/sub]]

For the first time in 400 years the borders of The Harmonious State are expanding outside of the main islands. Twelve new territories are being admitted into the Harmonious State, the territories of Haimong, Shizukawa, Kōryū, Daishin, Mizushima, Narashima, Hyotojima, Kazemori, Tsukijima, Hoshino, and Tategahama have been accepted as overseas Prefectures. With the Azusagawa Research Station being added as an overseas territory, as there are no permanent residents. Six of these twelve new territories are on the mainland of Kianzhou. There are three which are north of the large nation of Daesun, these are Haimong, Shizukawa, and Kōryū. There are also three which are south of Daesun, those being Daishin, Tategahama, and Hoshino. One of these new territories is on the continent of Argos, that being Kazemori. Finally the final four are islands. Those islands are Tsukijima, Mizushima, Narashima, and Hyotoshima. Hyotoshima is on the continent of Antarctica, where the Antarctic research stations will be founded. 

The National Police have already initiated a plan to rapidly oversee the deployment of trained officers to these new regions to assist with the training of existing Law Enforcement Officers in the region. This plan is in conjunction with a plan by the Ministry of Public Safety to send Medical Instructors, Paramedics, Firefighters, and other essential services into the region. The end goal of the Ministry of Public Safety is to ensure that all essential public safety services are operating at the level expected by the Government of the Harmonious State. All locals who are able to successfully pass their final skills exams and obtain an Aokajin license will be allowed to continue in their service. Those who do not will have to undergo academy training for their field of service in the Harmonious State to be eligible to return to their duties. Academies for the different services will be established in all of the new territories so that this process can be streamlined. 

Citizens in these new territories will have 175 days following the signing of the annexation proclamation to go to the Prefectural Administration Building and receive their Harmonious State Citizenship documents. There will also be documents there for individuals who wish to emigrate outside of the territory controlled by the Harmonious State. Individuals who wish to do so will not be stopped, but it is highly advisable for those individuals to fill out the Government paperwork and speak to a government representative prior to doing so. 

All citizens born prior to or on the date of the annexation proclamation in the new territories will be exempt from mandatory military service. All individuals born after the date of the annexation proclamation will have to register for their service in the Armed Forces of Aokashima when they turn eighteen (18) years old. However, all individuals who wish to volunteer for service in the new territories will be allowed to, provided they pass the necessary requirements and fitness tests. 

The admission of these new territories has also increased the number of seats in both the House of Representatives, and the Senate of The Harmonious State. The House of Representatives will now have four hundred and fifty (450) seats with the Senate having two hundred and fifty (250). All individuals who wish to vote in the Aokashima elections must register to vote as they are filling out their citizenship paperwork. There will be Government representatives at the Prefectural Administration buildings to ensure that all individuals who have questions will be helped in a quick and timely manner. 

[/spoiler]

[spoiler= The Expansion of the Aokajin Economy
[sub]Expansion Post Section IV[/sub]]

The annexation of the new overseas territories has given the Harmonious State access to more resources, these resources are Oil, Natural Gas, Gold, and Copper. These valuable resources will see much usage by the ever hungry economy of the Harmonious State. 

The Oil Industry is by far seeing the most substantial changes. For decades the Harmonious State has gotten its crude oil from offshore reserves and brought it back to the mainland for processing. But with the admission of the new overseas prefectures, oil will be extracted from onshore reserves as well.
